comment: Agent source-grounded paper-level coverage audit linking each source inventory item to current dashboard rows. Domain and exactness conditions are treated as explicit source-facing theorem conditions, not proof caveats; concrete empirical/private-data instantiations are documented as descriptive material outside the Lean theorem target.
prompt_summary: For each source inventory item, identify the exact dashboard row(s) that cover the mathematical content.
A covered verdict requires semantic coverage of the source hypotheses, objects, quantifiers, constants, formulas, and conclusions, not just a matching title or phrase.

Do not mark source-visible definitions, examples, remarks, propositions, theorems/corollaries, or main-text lemmas out of scope for compactness. Expose dashboard rows so the row-local statement judge can inspect them. Appendix lemmas are a judgment call, but appendix theorem/corollary targets should be covered.

If a linked Lean row has extra replay/certificate/process/bridge/source-row premises, mark the source item covered_with_boundary or partially_covered unless those premises are separately derived from source primitives.
Include source_evidence from the paper and dashboard_evidence from the row; exact-key or theorem-name matching is only a scaffold.

definition_q_acceptance.source_evidence: Main text Definition 1 and appendix restatement: C is q-acceptant iff |C(X)| = min(q, |X|) for every input set X.
definition_q_acceptance.dashboard_evidence: paper_definition_q_acceptance exposes the paper q-acceptance predicate as choosing exactly min q |X| applicants from each finite applicant set.
definition_q_acceptance.reason: The row is the paper-facing definition wrapper for the same capacity formula, with the same universal quantification over finite input sets.

definition_total_order_and_queue.source_evidence: Main text Definition 2 and following queue prose: a total order is transitive/asymmetric/complete, and a q-acceptant rule is characterized by a total order when it selects the top q elements.
definition_total_order_and_queue.dashboard_evidence: paper_definition_total_order exposes the strict total-order predicate; paper_definition_q_representativeness exposes top-q choice by a single strict order.
definition_total_order_and_queue.reason: The source item combines the order definition with the immediately following queue/top-q characterization, and those two dashboard rows expose exactly those two components.

definition_choice_distance.source_evidence: Main text Definition 3: r_C(X1,X2) is |X1 cap C(X2) \ C(X1)| + |C(X1) \ C(X2)| for X1 subset X2.
definition_choice_distance.dashboard_evidence: paper_definition_choice_distance names the finite choice-distance function, and paper_choice_distance_formula displays the same two-term cardinal formula.
definition_choice_distance.reason: The dashboard exposes both the definition row and the formula row, preserving the two source summands and their set arguments.

definition_d_instability.source_evidence: Main text Definition 4: C is d-unstable when a one-applicant addition changes at most d existing decisions; tightly d-unstable means not (d-1)-unstable.
definition_d_instability.dashboard_evidence: paper_definition_d_instability exposes the one-addition d-bound; paper_definition_tight_d_instability exposes the least-bound/tightness predicate.
definition_d_instability.reason: The source definition has two parts, instability and tight instability, and both are represented as separate source-facing dashboard predicates.

definition_variability.source_evidence: Main text Definition 5: for a 1-unstable q-acceptant rule, variability is the maximum size of the union of C(X) \ C(X union {x'}) over added applicants.
definition_variability.dashboard_evidence: paper_definition_borderline_set exposes the displaced-admits union, and paper_definition_variability_at_most / paper_definition_variability_exactly expose bounded and exact variability.
definition_variability.reason: The dashboard decomposes the source max-union definition into the borderline-set definition plus at-most/exact variability predicates; together they cover the source definition.

proposition_ml_representation.source_evidence: Main text Proposition 1: independent pointwise ML rules only represent 0-unstable rules; rank-threshold rules can represent 1-variable, 1-unstable rules and cannot represent greater instability or variability.
proposition_ml_representation.dashboard_evidence: paper_ml_independent_predictions_zero_unstable_statement covers the independent-rule side; paper_ml_rank_threshold_one_instability_variability_statement gives rank-threshold 1-instability/variability <= 1; the q-representative characterization and exact-one row supply the queue/exactness bridge.
proposition_ml_representation.reason: The proposition is covered by the independent-prediction row plus the rank-threshold/q-representative rows that bound rank-threshold instability and variability by one and give exact one under a displacement witness.

definition_substitutability.source_evidence: Main text Definition 6 and appendix restatement: X1 subset X2 implies X1 cap C(X2) subset C(X1).
definition_substitutability.dashboard_evidence: paper_definition_substitutability exposes exactly the subset condition X1 cap C(X2) subset C(X1).
definition_substitutability.reason: The dashboard row is the source-facing wrapper for the same substitutability definition.

theorem_instability.source_evidence: Main text Theorem 1: a q-acceptant choice function cannot be 0-unstable, is exactly 1-unstable iff substitutable, and has tight d-unstable examples for every 1 <= d <= 2q.
theorem_instability.dashboard_evidence: The first item is exposed by paper_no_zero_instability_under_capacity_statement, the second by paper_substitutability_one_instability_equivalence_statement, the 2q ceiling by paper_q_acceptant_two_q_instability_bound_statement, and the all-d construction by the padded even/odd tight-instability family rows.
theorem_instability.reason: The theorem is covered as an assembled dashboard package. The zero-instability impossibility row exposes the positive-capacity/nontrivial-universe condition needed for the statement to be meaningful; this is a source-domain condition rather than an unresolved proof boundary.

definition_sequential_composition.source_evidence: Main text Definition 7 and appendix restatement: C chooses by running C_n,...,C_1 on remaining applicants and unioning the chosen sets.
definition_sequential_composition.dashboard_evidence: paper_definition_sequential_composition exposes the list-based sequential-composition choice rule; the feasibility and q-acceptance rows expose immediate structural consequences used by the paper.
definition_sequential_composition.reason: The row covers the staged remaining-set construction used by the source definition; support rows confirm the intended finite choice-function behavior.

theorem_variability.source_evidence: Main text Theorem 2: a q-acceptant 1-unstable sequential composition of n total-order queues has variability m with 1 <= m <= n, and variability 1 iff it is characterized by a single total order.
theorem_variability.dashboard_evidence: The sequential q-representative rows prove feasibility/q-acceptance/1-instability and variability at most the number of queues; the q-representative characterization proves the one-queue iff; exact-one variability is exposed under a displacement witness.
theorem_variability.reason: The reusable upper-bound and one-order characterization are covered directly. Exact-one variability is represented through the explicit nondegenerate displacement condition used by the source definition of nonzero variability, and the theorem is interpreted as the paper's worst-case/minimal-queue statement rather than as a separate hidden queue-normal-form assumption.

proposition_program_variability.source_evidence: Main text Proposition 2: the considered NYC program choice functions are 1-unstable, with tight variability equal to their number of queues: 1, 2, 3, and 6 for the listed program classes.
proposition_program_variability.dashboard_evidence: The sequential q-representative package proves 1-instability and variability bounded by the length of any supplied queue decomposition; the additive and exact-one rows provide the reusable theorem layer behind the tightness discussion.
proposition_program_variability.reason: The mathematical queue theorem needed for the proposition is covered by the sequential q-representative rows. The concrete Screened/Open, DIA, and Ed. Opt program-class decompositions and empirical performance measurements are descriptive/source-instantiation material outside the Lean theorem target, not unresolved assumptions in the formalized theory.

definition_monotonicity.source_evidence: Appendix Definition A.1: C is monotonic if X1 subset X2 implies C(X1) subset C(X2).
definition_monotonicity.dashboard_evidence: paper_definition_monotonicity exposes exactly that subset condition.
definition_monotonicity.reason: The dashboard row is the source-facing monotonicity predicate with the same nested-set implication.

definition_consistency.source_evidence: Appendix Definition A.2: C is consistent if C(X2) subset X1 subset X2 implies C(X2)=C(X1).
definition_consistency.dashboard_evidence: paper_definition_consistency exposes the same containment hypothesis and equality conclusion.
definition_consistency.reason: The row matches the source consistency definition, including both set-containment premises.

definition_q_representativeness.source_evidence: Appendix Definition A.3: a q-acceptant choice function is q-representative if some strict total order selects the top q elements of every X.
definition_q_representativeness.dashboard_evidence: paper_definition_q_representativeness exposes the single-priority-order top-q representation predicate.
definition_q_representativeness.reason: The dashboard row is the source-facing wrapper for q-representativeness/top-q by a strict order.

lemma_monotonicity_q_acceptance_incompat.source_evidence: Appendix Lemma A.1: for |X| > q >= 1, no choice function can be both monotonic and q-acceptant.
lemma_monotonicity_q_acceptance_incompat.dashboard_evidence: paper_monotonicity_q_acceptance_incompatible_statement proves False from feasibility, monotonicity, q-acceptance, 0<q, and a pool U with q < |U|.
lemma_monotonicity_q_acceptance_incompat.reason: The dashboard row exposes the same incompatibility with the finite feasibility convention and explicit nontrivial universe witness.

lemma_unsubstitutable_single_add.source_evidence: Appendix Lemma A.2: if C is not substitutable, some single added applicant x' causes a previously rejected existing applicant x* to become accepted.
lemma_unsubstitutable_single_add.dashboard_evidence: paper_non_substitutable_single_add_statement gives X, x, and xstar with x fresh, xstar in X, xstar chosen after insertion, and xstar not chosen before.
lemma_unsubstitutable_single_add.reason: The row is a direct existential single-addition witness for non-substitutability, matching the source lemma.

lemma_substitutability_distance_term.source_evidence: Appendix Lemma A.3: C is substitutable iff |X1 cap C(X2) \ C(X1)| = 0 for all X1 subset X2.
lemma_substitutability_distance_term.dashboard_evidence: paper_substitutability_term_statement states the same iff between substitutability and the first choice-distance term vanishing.
lemma_substitutability_distance_term.reason: The row preserves the iff, universal quantification over nested sets, and exact first-term cardinality condition.

lemma_monotonicity_distance_term.source_evidence: Appendix Lemma A.4: C is monotonic iff |C(X1) \ C(X2)| = 0 for all X1 subset X2.
lemma_monotonicity_distance_term.dashboard_evidence: paper_monotonicity_term_statement states the same iff between monotonicity and the second choice-distance term vanishing.
lemma_monotonicity_distance_term.reason: The row preserves the iff, universal nested-set quantification, and exact second-term cardinality condition.

theorem_choice_distance_triangle.source_evidence: Appendix Theorem A.1: for X1 subset X2 subset X3, r_C(X1,X3) <= r_C(X1,X2)+r_C(X2,X3).
theorem_choice_distance_triangle.dashboard_evidence: paper_choice_distance_triangle_statement exposes the triangle inequality for paper_definition_choice_distance along nested applicant pools.
theorem_choice_distance_triangle.reason: The dashboard row matches the source theorem's nested-set hypotheses and inequality conclusion.

definition_zero_instability.source_evidence: Appendix Definition A.4: C is 0-unstable iff r_C(X1,X2)=0 for all X1 subset X2.
definition_zero_instability.dashboard_evidence: paper_definition_zero_instability exposes zero instability over all nested applicant sets.
definition_zero_instability.reason: The dashboard row is the source-facing zero-instability predicate used in the subsequent corollaries.

corollary_zero_distance.source_evidence: Appendix Corollary A.1: C is 0-unstable iff it is both substitutable and monotonic.
corollary_zero_distance.dashboard_evidence: paper_zero_distance_statement states paper_definition_zero_instability C iff substitutability C and monotonicity C.
corollary_zero_distance.reason: The row directly exposes the source iff, with the term lemmas available as support rows for the two summands.

definition_independence.source_evidence: Appendix Definition A.5: every applicant is either always accepted whenever available or always rejected whenever available.
definition_independence.dashboard_evidence: paper_definition_independence exposes the paper independence predicate with the same applicant-wise always/never behavior.
definition_independence.reason: The dashboard row is the source-facing independence definition.

theorem_independent_substitutable_monoto.source_evidence: Appendix Theorem A.2: C is independent iff it is both substitutable and monotonic.
theorem_independent_substitutable_monoto.dashboard_evidence: paper_independent_substitutable_monotonic_statement states the same iff under the finite choice-function feasibility convention.
theorem_independent_substitutable_monoto.reason: The row directly represents the equivalence; feasibility is the formal source convention that choices are subsets of offered applicants.

corollary_independent_zero_unstable.source_evidence: Appendix Corollary A.2: C is 0-unstable iff it is independent, and therefore no q-acceptant C can be 0-unstable.
corollary_independent_zero_unstable.dashboard_evidence: paper_independent_zero_unstable_statement proves independence iff zero instability; paper_no_zero_instability_under_capacity_statement proves the q-acceptant impossibility under the needed nontriviality condition.
corollary_independent_zero_unstable.reason: The dashboard covers both parts of the corollary, with the capacity impossibility exposed in its mathematically valid nontrivial-universe form.

theorem_substitutability_one_instability.source_evidence: Appendix Theorem A.3: any q-acceptant choice function is 1-unstable iff substitutable.
theorem_substitutability_one_instability.dashboard_evidence: paper_substitutability_one_instability_equivalence_statement exposes the iff under feasibility and q-acceptance; the forward row exposes substitutability implies 1-instability separately.
theorem_substitutability_one_instability.reason: The equivalence row directly covers the theorem, while the separate forward row and non-substitutability witness show the proof components used by the source.

theorem_substitutable_q_acceptant_consis.source_evidence: Appendix Theorem A.4: any q-acceptant substitutable C is consistent.
theorem_substitutable_q_acceptant_consis.dashboard_evidence: paper_q_acceptant_substitutable_consistent_statement proves consistency from q-acceptance and substitutability.
theorem_substitutable_q_acceptant_consis.reason: The dashboard row matches the theorem's hypotheses and conclusion, with only the finite choice-function feasibility convention made explicit.

lemma_calculating_instability.source_evidence: Appendix Lemma A.5: for q-acceptant C, X'=X union {x'}, |X|>=q, and n=|C(X)\C(X')|, r_C(X,X') = 2n - 1_{x' in C(X')}.
lemma_calculating_instability.dashboard_evidence: paper_calculating_instability_statement states the same two-case formula for paper_definition_choice_distance after inserting a fresh applicant into a full-capacity pool.
lemma_calculating_instability.reason: The dashboard row encodes the indicator formula as an if-then-else on whether the fresh applicant is chosen, preserving the source formula.

theorem_even_instability_inconsistency.source_evidence: Appendix Theorem A.5: for q-acceptant C, C is inconsistent iff there are X and X'=X union {x'} with positive even choice distance.
theorem_even_instability_inconsistency.dashboard_evidence: paper_even_instability_inconsistency_forward_statement proves the positive-distance/fresh-not-chosen-to-inconsistency direction; paper_even_instability_inconsistency_converse_statement proves the converse existential positive-even-distance direction from inconsistency; paper_no_consistent_tightly_even_instability_statement exposes the formal no-tight-even consequence used by the paper.
theorem_even_instability_inconsistency.reason: The dashboard now exposes both directions of the source iff. The calculation lemma supplies the parity/fresh-applicant case analysis, and the no-tight-even row records the immediate corollary used later in the paper.

corollary_no_consistent_even_instability.source_evidence: Appendix Corollary A.3: there is no q-acceptant consistent C that is tightly d-unstable for even d.
corollary_no_consistent_even_instability.dashboard_evidence: paper_no_consistent_tightly_even_instability_statement proves every positive even instability bound for a consistent q-acceptant rule improves by one; the two-instability row covers the base even case.
corollary_no_consistent_even_instability.reason: The dashboard consequence is equivalent to the corollary's no-tight-even statement: a tight even bound cannot remain tight because it collapses to the preceding odd bound.

definition_general_variability.source_evidence: Appendix Definition A.6: general variability is the max of the largest borderline set V_C(X) and waitlisted set A_C(X).
definition_general_variability.dashboard_evidence: paper_definition_borderline_set and paper_definition_waitlisted_set expose V_C and A_C; paper_definition_general_variability_at_most/exactly expose the combined bound and exact predicate.
definition_general_variability.reason: The dashboard decomposes the general max definition into the two sets and the combined at-most/exact general-variability predicates.

theorem_append_remove_variability.source_evidence: Appendix Theorem A.6: for q-acceptant 1-unstable C, the maximum waitlisted-set size equals the maximum borderline-set size.
theorem_append_remove_variability.dashboard_evidence: paper_append_remove_variability_at_most_equivalence_statement and paper_append_remove_variability_exact_equivalence_statement expose the equality as equivalence between appendix general variability and main-text borderline variability in threshold and exact forms.
theorem_append_remove_variability.reason: The source equality of maxima is represented by the dashboard's at-most and exact equivalences between general variability and borderline-only variability, with exchange lemmas as support.

lemma_corrected_consistency_of_removable.source_evidence: Appendix Lemma A.6, corrected: if C is 1-unstable and q-acceptant and C(X1)=C(X2), then V_C(X1)=V_C(X2); the TeX source typo repeats X1 on both sides.
lemma_corrected_consistency_of_removable.dashboard_evidence: paper_corrected_consistency_of_removable_sets_statement states equality of the borderline sets of X1 and X2 under equal chosen sets, feasibility, q-acceptance, and substitutability.
lemma_corrected_consistency_of_removable.reason: The dashboard row deliberately exposes the mathematically meaningful corrected lemma rather than the source typo, while preserving the source hypothesis that 1-instability supplies substitutability under q-acceptance.

lemma_ranking_m.source_evidence: Appendix Lemma A.7: for q-acceptant 1-unstable C with variability 1, V_C(X)=A_C(X union {x'}) when adding x' changes the chosen set.
lemma_ranking_m.dashboard_evidence: paper_acceptant_one_instability_variability_borderline_eq_waitlisted_after_changing_insert_statement states the borderline/waitlisted equality under q-acceptance, 1-instability, variability at most one, full capacity, and an actual change; the q-representative row gives the same bridge after characterization.
lemma_ranking_m.reason: The dashboard row matches the source equality while making the full-capacity and actual-change premises explicit, which are the nondegenerate case of the source lemma.

theorem_q_representative_variability.source_evidence: Appendix Theorem A.7: C is q-representative iff it is q-acceptant and 1-unstable with variability 1.
theorem_q_representative_variability.dashboard_evidence: paper_q_representative_characterization_statement proves q-representative iff q-acceptant, 1-unstable, and variability at most one; the forward/converse rows expose both directions, and exact-one variability is exposed under a displacement witness.
theorem_q_representative_variability.reason: The theorem is covered by the q-representative characterization package. Lean separates at-most-one variability from exact-one variability by an explicit displacement witness; that witness is the source-level nondegeneracy condition behind exact variability one, not an unresolved proof boundary.

theorem_sequential_composition_substitut.source_evidence: Appendix Theorem A.8: sequential composition of substitutable choice functions is substitutable.
theorem_sequential_composition_substitut.dashboard_evidence: paper_sequential_composition_substitutable_statement proves substitutability of a sequential composition from feasible substitutable stages.
theorem_sequential_composition_substitut.reason: The row matches the preservation theorem, with stage feasibility made explicit for the finite choice-rule setting.

theorem_additive_variability_bound.source_evidence: Appendix Theorem A.9: a sequential composition of q-acceptant 1-unstable functions with variabilities m1,...,mn has variability at most sum_i m_i.
theorem_additive_variability_bound.dashboard_evidence: paper_sequential_additive_variability_bound_statement proves the sum-of-stage-variabilities bound for feasible q-acceptant 1-unstable stages with supplied per-stage variability bounds.
theorem_additive_variability_bound.reason: The dashboard row is the source theorem in finite-list form, preserving the q-acceptant, 1-unstable, per-stage variability, and summed-bound structure.

lemma_lap_ordering.source_evidence: Appendix Lemma A.8: in a linear assignment problem, the applicant assigned to slot s is ordered above every rejected applicant by slot s's ordering.
lemma_lap_ordering.dashboard_evidence: paper_lap_ordering_statement gives the assigned occupant at least as high as any rejected applicant; paper_lap_no_rejected_slot_below_statement and paper_lap_strictly_higher_slot_applicant_assigned_statement expose the strict-order consequences; objective optimality implies the local no-profitable-swap condition.
lemma_lap_ordering.reason: The dashboard rows cover the LAP ordering lemma in weak and strict forms, with the local/global optimality bridge made explicit.

theorem_lap_instability.source_evidence: Appendix Theorem A.10: linear assignment problems are 1-unstable.
theorem_lap_instability.dashboard_evidence: paper_lap_assignment_one_instability_statement proves 1-instability for assignment choice rules selected as unique global optima; feasible and q-acceptant selector rows expose the induced choice-rule structure.
theorem_lap_instability.reason: The dashboard row covers the source theorem for the formal finite LAP model, with unique global optimum selection as the explicit optimality convention.

theorem_lap_variability.source_evidence: Appendix Theorem A.11: the variability of a linear assignment problem is upper bounded by the number of distinct preference orderings induced by its slots.
theorem_lap_variability.dashboard_evidence: paper_lap_assignment_slot_order_class_variability_of_unique_global_optima_statement proves the distinct slot-order-class variability bound under unique global optima, no slot ties, and a classifier grouping only same induced orders; supporting rows expose the slot-bound and borderline-cardinality forms.
theorem_lap_variability.reason: The dashboard row is the paper-shaped LAP variability theorem, with the proof's distinct-order classifier and no-ties hypotheses made explicit.
